title: A callout ring has one color, not two
goal: A zoom callout is drawn with a colored ring around it. That ring color can now be set in two different places that do not know about each other: the swatch in the toolbar while the callout tool is up, and a Border row in the Color section when the callout is picked. Pick one home for it so nobody has to wonder which one is the real one.
notes: Fallout from a-border-color-sits-with-the-other-colors: ColorSlot.border is on any layer with style.borderWidth > 0, and a callout defaults to a 3pt ring (ZoomCalloutBuilder.defaultStyle), so a picked callout now gets a Color section holding just Border. The toolbar path is EditorState.setCalloutBorderColor / EditorView.activeToolColorHex; the new path is setSelectionColor(slot: .border). Both perform one undo step and both write style.borderColorHex, so they agree on the value; what they do not share is any wording saying they are the same thing. Cheapest honest answer is probably to let the Color section be the home and have the toolbar swatch keep working as the tool default.
acceptance: Setting a picked callout ring color and setting it from the toolbar reach the same place and read the same value back
There is one obvious control for the ring color, and any second one is clearly the same control rather than a rival
A picked callout still shows its ring color somewhere, whichever answer is chosen
Nothing about the rest of the Color section changes

log.note: Adversarial review BEFORE building: the premise does not reproduce. Drew a callout in the probe and photographed it. With a callout picked there is exactly ONE ring colour control on screen, the Border row in the Color section. The tool bar swatch the task calls the rival never appears: it belongs to the tool in your hand (usesToolColor = an annotation or text tool), and setTool clears selectedLayerID for every tool but select, fill and the marquees. Confirmed in code and by a second walk that picked up the arrow tool with a callout selected: selection dropped and the swatch showed the arrow's own colour.

What the dead code actually cost: the popover's callout half was the ONLY host of the Magnification slider and the rectangle/circle Shape buttons. So a callout could be drawn and then never made bigger or made round. That is the real defect behind this task.

Built: (1) new Zoom Callout section in the dock (Sources/Photonz/CalloutInspector.swift, InspectorSectionID.callout, between Effects and Shadow) holding Magnification and Shape; (2) every callout branch stripped from EditorView's tool colour path and style popover, and calloutInspector/calloutShapeButton deleted; (3) EditorState.setCalloutBorderColor and setCalloutBorderWidth deleted (a callout's ring IS the layer's border, so colour goes through setSelectionColor(slot: .border) and width through the Effects Border slider); (4) selectedZoomCalloutLayer no longer insists on the select tool, so the section stays put like Color and Effects. Core (TDD): ZoomCalloutBuilder.magnificationRange, magnificationRange(including:), magnificationLabel, ZoomCalloutShape.title, plus a test pinning that a callout's only colour slot is .border. Two playtest actions added (magnifyCallout, roundCallout) so a walk can drive dock-only controls.

Verified live: Scripts/playtest/callout-ring-color-walk.json, probe with Screen Recording granted. Section shows Magnification 2.0x and Shape Rectangle|Circle; pulling to 4x grew the frame to 880x560 around its centre; Circle rounded the ring on canvas; the Color section's Border row repainted the ring crimson and read back; three undos put colour, shape and size back one step each. Scripts/test.sh green (2789 tests). Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-04-callout-one-home.json with three real screen captures.
